thread.title: Facebook is in bear market territory, Apple is in a correction, and they are far from alone

title: Facebook is in bear market territory, Apple is in a correction, and they are far from alone
text:
Published: Apr 2, 2018 3:25 p.m. ET Share 
Apple joins 70% of tech sector in correction territory, while about one in five tech companies are experiencing a bear market Getty Images Will Apple be the next tech stock tossed to the bears? 
By Wallace Witkowski Reporter 
After the worst quarter for stocks in more than two years and another decline at the beginning of a new quarter Monday, nearly a fifth of the S&P 500’s tech sector has slipped into bear territory, led by Facebook Inc.’s decline of more than 20%. 
About 70% of the sector, including Apple Inc. AAPL, -0.66% is in correction territory, with big names like Microsoft Corp. MSFT, -3.01% flirting with correction levels. Some big tech companies, like Google parent Alphabet Inc. GOOG, -2.45% GOOGL, -2.36% are already there and approaching bear levels. 
Read more about bear markets and corrections 
A bear market is defined as 20% or more off the stock’s 52-week high, while a correction is 10% or more off the 52-week high. Tech stocks have an increasingly large effect on stock indexes because of their weighting: The sector accounts for $6.473 trillion, or about 28%, of the S&P 500’s $23.438 trillion in market cap spread across 11 sectors, according to FactSet data. 
On Monday, 13 out of the tech 69 stocks on the S&P 500 index SPX, -2.23% were 20% or more off their 52-week high, or at bear levels. Company/ticker
